definition: PlainTalk is the collective name for several speech synthesis (MacinTalk) and speech recognition technologies developed by Apple Inc.
details: In 1990, Apple invested in speech recognition technology, hiring many researchers in the field. The result was "PlainTalk", released with the AV models in the Macintosh Quadra series from 1993. It was made a standard system component in System 7.1.2, and has since been shipped on all PowerPC, Intel, Apple silicon, and some 68k Macintoshes.

explainer.lead: PlainTalk is the collective name for Apple's speech synthesis and speech recognition technologies. It became a standard system component shipped across PowerPC, Intel, Apple silicon, and some 68k Macintoshes.

tiers.eli5: It is the set of voices and listening features built into Mac computers that let them speak and understand speech.
tiers.practitioner: Apple shipped it as a standard system component after releasing it with the Macintosh Quadra AV models in 1993.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a family of speech synthesis (MacinTalk) and speech recognition technologies rather than a single algorithm.

explainer.example: A Macintosh Quadra AV model shipped with PlainTalk, letting the machine speak using MacinTalk voices.
